3700: a primitive root; properly, to become pale, i.e. (by implication) to pine after; also to fear; (have) desire, be greedy, long, sore.
3701: from כָּסַף; silver (from its pale color); by implication, money; money, price, silver(-ling).
3702: (Aramaic) corresponding to כֶּסֶף; {silver (from its pale color); by implication, money}; money, silver.
3703: perhaps from כֶּסֶף; silvery; Casiphja, a place in Babylon; Casiphia.
3704: from כָּסָה; a cushion or pillow (as covering a seat or bed); pillow.
3706: (Aramaic) or כְּעֶת; (Aramaic), feminine of כְּעַן; thus (only in the formula 'and so forth'); at such a time.
3707: a primitive root; to trouble; by implication, to grieve, rage, be indignant; be angry, be grieved, take indignation, provoke (to anger, unto wrath), have sorrow, vex, be wroth.
3708: or (in Job) כַּעַשׂ; from כַּעַס; vexation; anger, angry, grief, indignation, provocation, provoking, [idiom] sore, sorrow, spite, wrath.
3709: from כָּפַף; the hollow hand or palm (so of the paw of an animal, of the sole, and even of the bowl of a dish or sling, the handle of a bolt, the leaves of a palm-tree); figuratively, power; branch, [phrase] foot, hand((-ful), -dle, (-led)), hollow, middle, palm, paw, power, sole, spoon.
3710: from כָּפַף; a hollow rock; rock.
3711: a primitive root; properly, to bend, i.e. (figuratively) to tame or subdue; pacify.
3712: feminine of כַּף; a leaf of a palmtree; branch.
3713: from כָּפַר; properly, a cover, i.e. (by implication) a tankard (or covered goblet); also white frost (as covering the ground); bason, hoar(-y) frost.
3714: from an unused root meaning to connect; a girder; beam.
3715: from כָּפַר; a village (as covered in by walls); also a young lion (perhaps as covered with a mane); (young) lion, village. Compare כָּפָר.
3716: feminine of כְּפִיר; the village (always with the art.); Kephirah, a place in Palestine; Chephirah.
3717: a primitive root; to fold together; figuratively, to repeat; double.
3719: a primitive root; to bend; bend.
3720: from כָּפַן; hunger (as making to stoop with emptiness and pain); famine.
3721: a primitive root; to curve; bow down (self).
3722: a primitive root; to cover (specifically with bitumen); figuratively, to expiate or condone, to placate or cancel; appease, make (an atonement, cleanse, disannul, forgive, be merciful, pacify, pardon, purge (away), put off, (make) reconcile(-liation).
3723: from כָּפַר; a village (as protected by walls); village. Compare כְּפִיר.
3724: from כָּפַר; properly, a cover, i.e. (literally) a village (as covered in); (specifically) bitumen (as used for coating), and the henna plant (as used for dyeing); figuratively, a redemption-price; bribe, camphire, pitch, ransom, satisfaction, sum of money, village.
3725: from כָּפַר; expiation (only in plural); atonement.
3726: from כָּפָר and עַמּוֹנִי, with the article interposed; village of the Ammonite; Kefar-ha-Ammoni, a place in Palestine; Chefarhaamonai.
3727: from כָּפַר; a lid (used only of the cover of the sacred Ark); mercy seat.
3728: a primitive root; to tread down; figuratively, to humiliate; cover.
3729: (Aramaic) a root of uncertain correspondence; to fetter; bind.
3730: or (Amos 9:1) כַּפְתּוֹר; probably from an unused root meaning to encircle; a chaplet; but used only in an architectonic sense, i.e. the capital of acolumn, or a wreath-like button or disk on the candelabrum; knop, (upper) lintel.
3731: or (Amos 9:7) כַּפְתּוֹר; apparently the same as כַּפְתֹּר; Caphtor (i.e. a wreath-shaped island), the original seat of the Philistines; Caphtor.
3732: patrial from כַּפְתֹּר; a Caphtorite (collectively) or native of Caphtor; Caphthorim, Caphtorim(-s).
3733: from כָּרַר in the sense of plumpness; a ram (as full-grown and fat), including a battering-ram (as butting); hence, a meadow (as for sheep); also a pad or camel's saddle (as puffed out); captain, furniture, lamb, (large) pasture, ram. See also בֵּית כַּר, כָּרִי.
3734: from the same as כּוּר; properly, a deep round vessel, i.e. (specifically) a cor or measure for things dry; cor, measure. Aramaic the same.
3735: (Aramaic) probably corresponding to כָּרָה in the sense of piercing(figuratively); to grieve; be grieved.
3736: from the same as כֶּבֶל; to gird or clothe; clothed.
3737: (Aramaic) from a verb corresponding to that of כַּרְבֵּל; a mantle; hat.
3738: a primitive root; properly, to dig; figuratively, to plot; generally, to bore or open; dig, [idiom] make (a banquet), open.
3739: usually assigned as a primitive root, but probably only a special application of כָּרָה (through the common idea of planning implied in a bargain); to purchase; buy, prepare.
3741: feminine of כַּר; a meadow; cottage.
3742: of uncertain derivation; a cherub or imaginary figure; cherub, (plural) cherubims.
3743: the same as כְּרוּב; Kerub, a place in Babylon; Cherub.
3745: (Aramaic) probably of Greek origin; to proclaim; make a proclamation.
3746: perhaps an abridged plural of כַּר in the sense of leader (of the flock); a life-guardsman; captains, Cherethites (from the margin).
3747: from כָּרַת; a cut; Kerith, a brook of Palestine; Cherith.
3748: from כָּרַת; a cutting (of the matrimonial bond), i.e. divorce; divorce(-ment).
3749: expanded from the same as כַּבּוֹן; a rim or top margin; compass.
3750: probably of foreign origin; the crocus; saffron.
3751: of foreign derivation; Karkemish, a place in Syria; Carchemish.
3752: of Persian origin; Karkas, a eunuch of Xerxes; Carcas.
3753: from כָּרַר; a dromedary (from its rapid motion as if dancing); swift beast.
3754: from an unused root of uncertain meaning; a garden or vineyard; vines, (increase of the) vineyard(-s), vintage. See also בֵּית הַכֶּרֶם.
3755: active participle of an imaginary denominative from כֶּרֶם; a vinedresser; vine dresser (as one or two words).
3756: from כֶּרֶם; gardener; Karmi, the name of three Israelites; Carmi.
3757: patronymically from כַּרְמִי; a Karmite or descendant of Karmi; Carmites.
3758: probably of foreign origin; carmine, a deep red; crimson.
3759: from כֶּרֶם; a planted field (garden, orchard, vineyard or park); by implication, garden produce; full (green) ears (of corn), fruitful field (place), plentiful (field).
3760: the same as כַּרְמֶל; Karmel, the name of a hill and of a town in Palestine; Carmel, fruitful (plentiful) field, (place).
3761: patron from כַּרְמֶל; a Karmelite or inhabitant of Karmel (the town); Carmelite.
3762: feminine of כַּרְמְלִי; a Karmelitess or female inhabitant of Karmel; Carmelitess.
3763: of uncertain derivation; Keran, an aboriginal Idumaean; Cheran.
3764: (Aramaic) corresponding to כִּסֵּא; a throne; throne.
3765: from כָּסַם; to lay waste; waste.
3766: a primitive root; to bend the knee; by implication, to sink, to prostrate; bow (down, self), bring down (low), cast down, couch, fall, feeble, kneeling, sink, smite (stoop) down, subdue, [idiom] very.
3767: from כָּרַע; the leg (from the knee to the ankle) of men or locusts (only in the dual); leg.
3768: of foreign origin; byssus or fine vegetable wool; green.
3769: a primitive root; to dance (i.e. whirl); dance(-ing).
3770: by variation from קָרַס; the paunch or belly (as swelling out); belly.
3771: of foreign origin; Karshena, a courtier of Xerxes; Carshena.
3772: a primitive root; to cut (off, down or asunder); by implication, to destroy or consume; specifically, to covenant (i.e. make an alliance or bargain, originally by cutting flesh and passing between the pieces); be chewed, be con-(feder-) ate, covenant, cut (down, off), destroy, fail, feller, be freed, hew (down), make a league (covenant), [idiom] lose, perish, [idiom] utterly, [idiom] want.
3773: passive participle feminine of כָּרַת; something cut, i.e. a hewn timber; beam.
3774: probably from כָּרַת in the sense of executioner; (compare טַבָּח) (only collectively in the singular as plural); a Kerethite or life-guardsman; Cherethims, Cherethites.
3775: apparently by transposition for כֶּבֶשׂ; a young sheep; lamb.
3776: feminine of כֶּשֶׂב; a young ewe; lamb.
3777: from an unused root of uncertain meaning; Kesed, a relative of Abraham; Chesed.
3778: (occasionally with enclitic) כַּשְׂדִּימָה; towards the Kasdites into Chaldea), patronymically from כֶּשֶׂד (only in the plural); a Kasdite, or descendant of Kesed; by implication, a Chaldaean (as if so descended); also an astrologer (as if proverbial of that people; Chaldeans, Chaldees, inhabitants of Chaldea.
3779: (Aramaic) corresponding to כַּשְׂדִּי; a Chaldaean or inhabitant of Chaldaea; by implication, a Magian or professional astrologer; Chaldean.
3780: a primitive root; to grow fat (i.e. be covered with flesh); be covered. Compare כָּסָה.
3781: from כָּשַׁל; properly, a feller, i.e. an axe; ax.
3782: a primitive root; to totter or waver (through weakness of the legs, especially the ankle); by implication, to falter, stumble, faint or fall; bereave (from the margin), cast down, be decayed, (cause to) fail, (cause, make to) fall (down, -ing), feeble, be (the) ruin(-ed, of), (be) overthrown, (cause to) stumble, [idiom] utterly, be weak.
3783: from כָּשַׁל; properly, a tottering, i.e. ruin; fall.
3784: a primitive root; properly, to whisper aspell, i.e. to inchant or practise magic; sorcerer, (use) witch(-craft).
3787: a primitive root properly, to be straight or right; by implication, to be acceptable; also to succeed or prosper; direct, be right, prosper.
3788: from כָּשֵׁר; success, advantage; equity, good, right.
3789: a primitive root; to grave, by implication, to write (describe, inscribe, prescribe, subscribe); describe, record, prescribe, subscribe, write(-ing, -ten).
3790: (Aramaic) corresponding to כָּתַב; {to grave, by implication, to write (describe, inscribe, prescribe, subscribe)}; write(-ten).
3791: from כָּתַב; something written, i.e. a writing, record or book; register, scripture, writing.
3792: (Aramaic) corresponding to כָּתָב; {something written, i.e. a writing, record or book}; prescribing, writing(-ten).
3793: from כָּתַב; a letter or other mark branded on the skin; [idiom] any (mark).
3794: or כִּתִּיִּי; patrial from an unused name denoting Cyprus (only in the plural); a Kittite or Cypriote; hence, an islander in general, i.e. the Greeks or Romans on the shores opposite Palestine; Chittim, Kittim.
3795: from כָּתַת; beaten, i.e. pure (oil); beaten.
3796: from an unused root meaning to compact; a wall (as gathering inmates); wall.
3797: (Aramaic) corresponding to כֹּתֶל; {a wall (as gathering inmates)}; wall.
3798: lemma כְּתִלִישׁ first two vowels, corrected to כִּתְלִישׁ; from כֹּתֶל and אִישׁ; wall of a man; Kithlish, a place in Palestine; Kithlish.
3799: a primitive root; properly, to carve or engrave, i.e. (by implication) to inscribe indelibly; mark.
